original_title: Photocatalytic Radical Relay Cyclization of N -Allyl Hydrazones with Diazo Compounds: Access to Ester-Containing and Fluorinated Dihydropyrazoles
title: Diazo radicals add onto hydrazones to build dihydropyrazoles
blurb: Photocatalysis generates carbon radicals from diazo compounds via a PCET-like step, which add across the C=C of N-allyl hydrazones and then cyclize shut into dihydropyrazoles, ester-bearing and fluorinated versions included. Runs in greener solvents with low diazo loading, which matters given how little of that stuff you want sitting around.

original_title: Development and preclinical evaluation of CP021, a CD38-targeted cyclic peptide radiotheranostic platform for multiple myeloma
title: A cyclic peptide theranostic for the myeloma lesions that hide in bone marrow
blurb: CP021 targets CD38 on malignant plasma cells, paired up as a Ga-68 PET tracer for imaging and a Lu-177 version for irradiating the same lesions. The point is catching the small, scattered myeloma deposits that are hard to spot and harder to hit. Preclinical only so far.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Enantioselective C(sp 3 )–C(sp 3 ) Radical Coupling Through Photoinduced Electron Donor–Acceptor Activation
title: Pairing two radicals without losing track of which hand each one offers
blurb: Coupling two transient alkyl radicals selectively is hard enough without demanding stereocontrol too. A chiral nickel catalyst and a double electron donor-acceptor activation get it done, building C(sp3)-C(sp3) bonds enantioselectively to make alpha-fluoroalkylated secondary alcohols, with one radical coming off a carboxylic acid precursor.

original_title: Late‐Stage Synthesis of Photoaffinity Labeling Probes via Photochemical Minisci Chemistry
title: Late-stage Minisci chemistry bolts photoaffinity handles onto finished drugs
blurb: Photoaffinity probes need a photocrosslinker and a bioorthogonal handle attached without disturbing the drug's active warhead. This route uses photochemical Minisci chemistry to install both late-stage, directly onto the parent molecule rather than rebuilding it from early intermediates.

original_title: Chiral cobalt-catalysed electrochemical enantioselective C–P coupling via phosphinoyl radicals
title: Cobalt electrocatalysis finally gets phosphinoyl radicals to behave
blurb: Phosphinoyl radicals have long resisted stereocontrol. A cobalt-mediated electrocatalytic setup couples them to carbon enantioselectively, giving access to P(V)-stereogenic compounds without needing a separate stoichiometric oxidant to drive the reaction.

original_title: Interfacial Electronic Coupling of Iron Nanoclusters on Cobalt-Modified Black Phosphorus for Electrocatalytic Nitrogen Reduction
title: Iron clusters on phosphorus try to out-compete hydrogen evolution for nitrogen reduction
blurb: Electrochemical nitrogen reduction usually loses the race to the easier hydrogen evolution side reaction. Growing Fe nanoclusters on Co-modified black phosphorus, Co added during exfoliation and Fe deposited after, gives smaller, more uniform clusters with stronger Fe-P electronic coupling, which is the lever being pulled to favor N2 over H2.

original_title: Long‐Lived Fluorinated Foldamer Channels Conduct Protons Through a Plausible Confined Carbonyl–Water Relay
title: A fluorinated channel that moves protons and keeps everything else out
blurb: These aromatic amide foldamers fold into transmembrane channels about 2.0 Å wide, narrow enough to exclude water and ions while still shuttling protons fast: 196.2 pS single-channel conductance, EC50 of 40 nM, open states lasting up to 170 seconds. Most artificial proton channels leak something; the exclusion here is the actual trick.

original_title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
title: An evolved photoenzyme that forces electrocyclization to go one way
blurb: Thermal 6π-electrocyclizations turn up in biosynthesis, but enzyme-catalyzed versions are rare and nobody really knows what makes one work. Ten mutations turned a [2+2]-cyclase into PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3, which runs antarafacial 6π-electrocyclizations on acrylanilide substrates in high yield by physically constraining how the substrate can sit in the pocket.

original_title: Biocatalytic Process Design for Efficient Cyanide-Free Production of the Industrial Specialty Chemical 4-Phenylbenzonitrile in Water at Low Temperature
title: Making 4-phenylbenzonitrile without the cyanide or the gas-phase furnace
blurb: Ammoxidation, the standard route to aromatic nitriles, is energy-hungry and struggles with bulky, high-boiling substrates like 4-phenylbenzonitrile. This biocatalytic process runs in water at low temperature instead, cutting cyanide out entirely for an industrially relevant specialty chemical.

original_title: Bioinspired Diversification of Short Peptides via Tyrosine Umpolung.
title: Flipping tyrosine's reactivity to diversify peptides
blurb: Tyrosine usually plays the nucleophile in a peptide; this flips its polarity so it acts as an electrophile instead, opening a new handle for tweaking short peptides late in the game at a residue that's normally off limits.

original_title: SnCl 4 ‐Assisted Spirol Catalysis for Stereoselective Cationic Polymerization of Vinyl Ethers
title: Tin plus a chiral diol teaches vinyl ethers to line up isotactic
blurb: A cheap Lewis acid-Brønsted acid combo, commercial SnCl4 paired with chiral spirobiindane diol (spirol), pushes cationic vinyl ether polymerization toward isotactic-rich chains. The actual acid doing the work looks to be the diol's phenolic proton, just activated by complexing with the tin, so SnCl4 is more of an enabler than the star.

original_title: Synthesis of Apo-Carotenal- and Retinal-Derived Esters and Amides for Probing Lecithin:Retinol Acyltransferase
title: Retinoid probes built to find out what actually makes LRAT bind
blurb: A matched set of retinoid- and apo-carotenoid-derived haloacetates and haloacetamides, built to tease apart whether LRAT inhibition comes down to electrophile reactivity, polyene chain length, or linkage type. The longer-conjugation analogs were so unstable they needed low-temperature coupling and chromatography-free purification just to isolate, which tells you how fragile these probes are to begin with.

original_title: A TME-Selective PEGylated Anti-Mesothelin Nanobody Unmasked by Single-Cell Antigen-Specificity Profiling in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
title: Mesothelin on pancreatic cancer wasn't actually tumor-selective
blurb: Single-cell RNA-seq across three PDAC cohorts finds mesothelin expressed at similar per-cell rates on tumor ductal cells (46-68%) and normal ductal cells (29-58%); the tumor enrichment everyone's been seeing in bulk data is just more duct cells in the sample, not more antigen per cell. Their answer is a PEGylated anti-mesothelin nanobody that only engages within the tumor microenvironment, since the antigen itself isn't giving you selectivity for free.

original_title: Chemoselective Electrochemical Ring Cleavage of Naphthols Enabling Structural Diversification
title: Cracking open naphthols' aromatic ring electrochemically
blurb: An electrochemical dearomatization method cleaves a core C-C bond in beta-naphthols, something their aromatic stability usually forbids, converting them into stereodefined, ring-opened esters. Those get reconstructed into a range of carbocycles and heterocycles, so the ring-cleavage is really a detour toward new skeletons rather than an end in itself.

original_title: Benzo-Fused Benzo[ mno ]aceanthrylene Isomers with Tunable Ground States: Toward a Diradicaloid Indeno[2,1,7,6- defg ]tetracene
title: One of these three diradicaloids decided to go open-shell
blurb: Three benzo-fused benzo[mno]aceanthrylene isomers all show redox amphoterism, but only indeno[2,1,7,6-defg]tetracene settles into an open-shell singlet ground state with real diradical character, backed by NMR/EPR and DFT. It's also the one with the smallest singlet-triplet gap and the most red-shifted UV-vis-NIR absorption of the set, so the diradical character isn't just a footnote, it's tied to the whole electronic profile.

original_title: Metal Cation-Free, Acidic CO2 Electroreduction Enabled by Non-Zero-Valent Metal Centers
title: Swapping out the alkali cations CO2 reduction usually needs
blurb: Acidic CO2-to-CO electroreduction normally leans on alkali metal cations to stabilize the *CO2- intermediate, but those cations precipitate salts and flood real electrolyzers. Here non-zero-valent metal centers in molecular and single-atom catalysts do that stabilizing job instead, run in a Nafion membrane electrode assembly, which also dodges the CO2 crossover that comes with the usual alkaline microenvironment.

original_title: Selenoxanthylyl radicals – characterization and conPET catalysis
title: Characterizing the radical selenoxanthylium photocatalysts leave behind
blurb: Selenoxanthylium photocatalysts get reductively quenched mid-cycle into persistent selenoxanthylyl radicals; this pins down what those radicals actually look like via EPR, cyclic voltammetry, UV-Vis, and TD-DFT, then puts them to work driving consecutive photoinduced electron-transfer catalysis. Useful if you want low-energy-photon photoredox without guessing at the resting state.

original_title: Novel B7-H3 Targeted Radiopharmaceutical Suppresses Tumor Growth in Preclinical Lung Cancer Models - Bioengineer.org
title: A B7-H3 radiopharmaceutical holds up in mouse lung cancer
blurb: A new B7-H3 targeted radiopharmaceutical slows tumor growth in preclinical lung cancer models. Preclinical only, so file it under promising mice, not promising patients yet.

original_title: Metal-Free Photoredox Hydrosulfonylation of gem -Difluoroallenes for the Direct Construction of α-CF2H Vinyl Sulfones
title: Eosin Y turns difluoroallenes into CF2H vinyl sulfones, no metal needed
blurb: Visible light and eosin Y drive sulfonyl chlorides to add across gem-difluoroallenes, with (TMS)3SiH mopping up the radical, delivering alpha-CF2H vinyl sulfones in good yield with high regio- and E-selectivity. Works across aryl, alkyl, and heteroaryl sulfonyl chlorides, and the mechanism checks out as a radical addition, the sulfonyl radical hitting the allene's beta carbon first.

original_title: Second-Generation Route Development and Scale-Up for the Synthesis of (1 R ,3 R )-3-(3,5-Bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl)-2,2-dichlorocyclopropane Carboxylic Acid
title: A second swing at making this dichlorocyclopropane acid at kilo scale
blurb: Gen one worked but was pricey, needed a low-yielding single-diastereomer split, and too many isolations. Gen two fixes most of that by reoptimizing the bis-arylative Heck coupling, swapping out the acetate leaving group, and reordering the steps. Not glamorous chemistry, but it's the paper you write once you actually have to deliver kilograms of the stuff.

original_title: Injectable Hydrogels for Programmable Protein Release
title: Hydrogels built to release different proteins on different schedules
blurb: Dextran-oxanorbornadiene/PEG-thiol hydrogels where the same crosslinker also tethers the protein cargo, so both hydrolysis and Michael-addition chemistry gate the release. The actual ask here is programmable kinetics that hold up across proteins of different sizes, which is exactly where depot gels usually fall apart.

original_title: A Unique Conformationally Assisted [2+2] Configuration in Cycloparaphenylenes Enables Efficient Laser Devices
title: Carbon nanorings pulling laser duty
blurb: [12]cycloparaphenylene and a stiffer stilbene-laced macrocycle both work as gain media in distributed feedback lasers, through a four-state cycle where excited-state distortion splits two delocalized states into two localized ones. The catch in the title is the real finding: it's specifically that [2+2] configuration doing the work, not macrocycles in general.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: DMF-Mediated Appel-Type Direct Deoxyfluorination of Glycosyl Hemiacetals
title: Turning sugar hemiacetals straight into glycosyl fluorides
blurb: An Appel-type deoxyfluorination, Ph3P, 1,2-diiodoethane, and KHF2 in DMF, that skips the usual exotic fluorinating reagents and routes through a glycosyl imidate intermediate instead. Mild, metal-free, good alpha-selectivity, scales up, and works for 18F labeling too, so there's a PET-tracer angle sitting right there.

original_title: Ultrasensitive Protein Detection and Imaging Mass Spectrometry Using Photocleavable Mass Tag-Based Signal Amplification
title: Borrowing DNA amplification to make protein mass spec more sensitive
blurb: Intact proteins ionize poorly and give weak, inconsistent signals in tissue sections, so this bolts hybridization chain reaction onto photocleavable mass tags to amplify signal before it ever hits the detector. If it holds up on real tissue, it's a fix for the actual chronic weak point in protein imaging MS, not small-molecule MS tricks repackaged.

original_title: Tag‐Enabled Recycling of Axially Chiral Iridium(III) Porphyrin Catalysts for Asymmetric Carbene Transfer
title: Give the iridium catalyst a fatty tail so you can fish it back out
blurb: C4-symmetric axially chiral Ir(III) porphyrins carrying four long alkyl chains, built so the metal can be recovered and reused instead of binned after one run. Iridium is neither abundant nor cheap, so recyclability is the actual pitch, and the tagged catalysts hold onto their activity and enantioselectivity in both cyclopropanation and C–H insertion.

original_title: Predicting Asymmetric Organocatalysis via Machine-Learning-Driven Molecular Dynamics of Chiral Deep Eutectic Solvents
title: Modeling why some chiral solvents make better catalysts than others
blurb: ML-driven molecular dynamics plus DFT on chiral deep eutectic solvents, trying to pin down what actually governs their performance as catalytic platforms rather than just green media. The headline so far: too much persistent structural ordering in the DES hurts catalysis, which, if it generalizes, is an actual design rule instead of the usual trial and error.

original_title: Genetic Code Expansion with Chalcogenated Tyrosines Tunes the Color and Noncovalent Interactions in Fluorescent Proteins
title: Swapping oxygen for sulfur and selenium in the GFP chromophore
blurb: Genetic code expansion installs chalcogen-substituted tyrosines, O, S, Se, right at the chromophore position in GFP, and walking down the periodic table red-shifts the fluorescence step by step while reshaping excited-state proton transfer and noncovalent contacts. A clean atom-by-atom dial for chromophore engineering rather than a one-off mutant.

original_title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H 2 O 2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
title: Locking COF backbones flat to stop electron-hole recombination
blurb: Covalent organic frameworks for coupled H2O2 photosynthesis and organic valorization usually bleed efficiency to fast electron-hole recombination. Borrowing the rigidity peptide bonds get for free, a fused-ring linker locks backbone rotation across a series of COFs with progressively more locking, making the frameworks flatter and more conjugated. More planarity tracking with better charge separation is the expected story, but it's nice to see someone actually build the series to prove it.

original_title: Synthesis of Chiral Tertiary Propargylic Alcohols by Using Dual Catalytic Activity of Halohydrin Dehalogenases
title: Enzymes doing double duty on propargylic alcohols
blurb: Halohydrin dehalogenases running two separate catalytic activities in the same pot to build chiral tertiary propargylic alcohols. Posted as a ChemRxiv preprint, so it's worth watching for yields and scope once it clears review.

original_title: Electrochemical Oxygen Reduction to Hydrogen Peroxide in Pure Water Using Cationic Polymer Modified Membrane Electrode Assembly
title: Making H2O2 out of nothing but water and electricity
blurb: A cationic polymer coating on the membrane electrode assembly to push the 2-electron oxygen reduction toward peroxide using pure deionized water, no electrolyte needed. The whole point is clearing that stubborn 40% Faraday efficiency wall that's dogged on-demand H2O2 electrosynthesis.

original_title: Dynamic (68)Ga‑PSMA‑11 PET reveals blood-brain barrier permeability as the primary driver of tracer uptake in glioma: a pharmacokinetic modeling study.
title: That PSMA PET signal in gliomas might just be a leaky blood-brain barrier
blurb: Dynamic 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET plus pharmacokinetic modeling finds that uptake in glioma tracks blood-brain barrier permeability, not necessarily PSMA expression itself. Worth sitting with if you've been reading glioma PSMA scans as a direct readout of target density.

original_title: Machine Learning in Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Catalysis: Complementary Strengths across Scales
title: Why ML works great on one kind of catalysis and shrugs at the other
blurb: A perspective arguing homogeneous catalysis is the better playground for experimental ML, discrete catalysts, clean descriptors, real HTE pipelines, while heterogeneous catalysis has mostly paid off for the computational side instead. A structural explanation for why the two literatures feel so lopsided.

original_title: Selective Methyl Substitution and Transfer in an NNN-Supported Dialuminum Complex
title: Picking off one methyl group at a time on a dialuminum complex
blurb: A bridging and terminal methyl pair on an NNN dialuminum(III) complex, and it turns out the bridging one is the reactive handle: swap it for chloride with TMSCl, add it across an aldehyde to make a new C-C bond, or deprotonate C-H/P-H bonds with it. Selective Al-C chemistry where you'd expect a mess.

original_title: Synthesis of Spiro‐Pyrazolone‐Oxadiazoles via 1,3 Dipole Cycloaddition of Pyrazole‐Diones With Nitrile Imines
title: Spiro pyrazolone-oxadiazoles, built by cycloaddition
blurb: Nitrile imines plus pyrazole-diones in a 1,3-dipolar cycloaddition give spiro scaffolds fusing two five-membered azaheterocycles, simple to run and scalable with decent functional group tolerance. The enzyme-inhibitor angle is just an online activity prediction so far, not an actual assay.

original_title: Nickel‐Catalyzed Enantio‐ and Regioselective Addition of Silicon and Boron Nucleophiles to Methylene Cyclobutene for the Construction of Quaternary Stereocenters
title: Nickel catalysis puts silicon and boron on the same diene, your choice which
blurb: A nickel catalyst adds Si-B or B-B reagents across the diene of methylenecyclobutenes, landing either a silicon-substituted or boron-substituted quaternary stereocenter on the ring with up to 99% ee and strong regiocontrol. First catalytic asymmetric route to the silicon version of these cyclobutanes.

original_title: System-Independent Retention Index Prediction via Multimodal Molecular Representation Learning
title: Predicting LC retention index straight from structure, no instrument required
blurb: MultiModal-RI pairs a graph neural network with an RBF-Kolmogorov-Arnold layer to predict retention index from molecular structure alone, aimed at the chronic metabolomics problem of having way more candidate structures than reference RI values. A computational fix for a very specific bottleneck in untargeted metabolite ID.

original_title: A Phosphinidene‐Bridged P 6 Platform for Phosphorus Framework Editing, Fragment Transfer, and Derivatization
title: Turning white phosphorus into a reusable P6 LEGO set
blurb: A phosphinidene bridge converts P4 into a hexaphosphane that isn't just another P4-derived curiosity, it's a platform you can reorganize, strip back to P4, transfer phosphinidene units from, or insert heteroelements into. Controlled framework editing on an element that usually just reacts and sits there.

original_title: Micelle-Driven MOF Degradation for Enhanced Cargo Release in Micromotors
title: Getting a MOF to fall apart on purpose, for once
blurb: Anionic surfactant micelles pull Cu2+ straight out of HKUST-1, which normally counts as the framework failing, but here it's harnessed to dump cargo out of micromotors faster. The degradation depends on how the surfactants self-assemble and how exposed the metal nodes are, so it's a controllable failure mode rather than a happy accident.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photo‐aerobic Oxidation/Tandem Cyclization Enabled by a Novel Photocatalyst: Metal‐Free Synthesis of Chiral Pyrrolidines
title: A metal-free way to oxidize benzylic C-H bonds without torching the amine next door
blurb: A new bifunctional photocatalyst built on proton-coupled electron transfer does aerobic benzylic oxidation on amino alkyl arenes, a substrate class that usually gets its amine oxidized instead of the C-H bond you wanted. Feeds into a tandem cyclization that delivers chiral pyrrolidines with no metal catalyst involved.

original_title: Regio- and Enantioselective Allylboration of 1,3-Dienes
title: Cu/Pd tag team puts the boron exactly where you want it on a diene
blurb: A Cu/Pd synergistic catalysis allylboration of acyclic 1,3-dienes that nails regio-, enantio-, and E-selectivity all at once, delivering chiral allylboron-containing 1,5-dienes. Those feed straight into chiral cyclopentenes with multiple stereocenters, so it reads less as a new reaction and more as a shortcut to a whole class of building blocks people have been assembling the hard way.

original_title: Endogenous Metabolite-Mediated Alterations of Drug Ion Intensity in Electrospray Ionization across LC-ESI-MS and DESI-MSI
title: Your mass spec's drug signal depends on what else is in the tissue
blurb: LC-ESI-MS and DESI-MSI readings for DMT, 5-MeO-DMT, cocaine, and ketamine in mouse tissue and biofluids shift depending on the endogenous metabolites sitting in the matrix, and how much depends on both the drug and the tissue. Matrix effects in ESI aren't new, but this is a concrete reminder that quantitation is only as good as the background you didn't control for.

original_title: Growth Factor Ligand Functionalization Enhances Cellular and In Vivo Uptake of DNA Nanodevices.
title: Tag a DNA nanodevice with a growth factor and cells take it up better
blurb: Functionalizing DNA nanodevices with a growth factor ligand boosts both cellular and in vivo uptake. That's about all there is here, but it's a simple handle on a delivery problem that's dogged DNA nanostructures for a while.

original_title: Temporal changes in FAPI uptake in subcutaneous U87MG xenografts progression: implications for preclinical FAP-targeted imaging and therapy
title: FAP expression in a tumor xenograft isn't a fixed target, it drifts
blurb: Longitudinal PET/CT with two different Ga-68 FAPI tracers in U87MG xenografts, backed by biodistribution, autoradiography, immunohistochemistry, co-culture, and pharmacological/theranostic interventions, tracks how FAP expression changes as the tumor progresses. The takeaway for anyone running FAP-targeted imaging or therapy off this same model: the signal window depends on when you image, not just whether the target is there.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Reengineering ELISA through Solid-Phase Transfer: A Wash-Free 3D Pillar-Array Immunoassay for Clothianidin Detection
title: Skip the washing step, keep the ELISA
blurb: A new anti-clothianidin monoclonal antibody with cross-reactivity under 0.1% against nine other neonicotinoids, paired with a 3D pillar-array format that moves the assay to solid phase instead of washing it there. A tighter antibody plus a wash-free format is the combo that actually gets you a field-deployable pesticide test instead of another lab-only ELISA.

original_title: Nanoscale Flexibility Enables Low-Enthalpy Cooperative Water Sorption
title: A MOF that breathes instead of fighting humidity swings
blurb: Cu(1,2,3-triazolate)2 nanoparticles under 120 nm keep enough flexibility at the Cu2+ centers to expand and contract with humidity, so uptake happens via a low-enthalpy "breathing" mode rather than tight binding. That's exactly what atmospheric water harvesters need: a sorbent that regenerates without having to be baked.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
title: Mixing five more cations into a perovskite flips its iron's spin state
blurb: Loading La0.7Sr0.3FeO3 up into a six-cation entropy-stabilized perovskite switches the B-site Fe from high-spin to low-spin, which strengthens Fe-O d-p hybridization and knocks down the barriers for high-temperature oxygen evolution. A genuine mechanistic lever on spin state, not just another throw-more-elements-at-it entropy paper.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: 2-Ferrocenyl-Phosphinine: Synthesis, Coordination Chemistry, and Properties
title: A ferrocene-flavored phosphinine, built by kicking out CO2
blurb: A ferrocenyl phosphaalkyne plus 2-pyrone in a [4+2] cycloaddition releases CO2 and leaves behind a new 2-ferrocenyl-phosphinine, bulkier by %Vbur than earlier 2-substituted phosphinines and redox-active on top of that. It coordinates cleanly to Au(I), Cu(I), Rh(I), and group 6 metal precursors, more a general-purpose bulky ligand than one tuned for a single job.

original_title: Synthesis of a hydroxy-functionalized poly(m-xylylene) via visible-light-driven reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde using perylene as a photoredox catalyst
title: Light and a dye photocatalyst turn an aldehyde into a hydroxylated polymer
blurb: Perylene as a photoredox catalyst under blue light drives reductive coupling of isophthalaldehyde into a hydroxy-functionalized poly(m-xylylene), and the Hantzsch ester matters specifically because it hydrogen-bonds to activate the aldehyde, which is what lets the chain actually grow. MALDI-TOF on the chain ends shows the structure depends on exactly how that polymerization ran, so this lands more as a methods result than a new material.

original_title: Ancestors of Arylmalonate Decarboxylase Show Increased Activity, Stability, and Stereoselectivity
title: Older versions of a decarboxylase enzyme beat the modern one
blurb: Ancestral sequence reconstruction of arylmalonate decarboxylase turns up ancestors that beat the extant Bordetella enzyme on stability, on substrate range for the alkenyl substituents it used to choke on, and on stereoselectivity. Going backwards through the phylogeny to fix an enzyme's practical flaws, rather than forward with directed evolution, is the actual trick here.

original_title: Effects of microgravity on the photoelectrodeposition of Rh electrocatalyst nanoparticles and on the diffusion coefficient of the Rh 3+ ions in the precursor electrolyte
title: Even rhodium catalysts get tested off-world now
blurb: Checking whether photoelectrodepositing rhodium nanoparticles onto p-InP, the trick that lowers the overpotential for hydrogen evolution, still works without gravity, plus tracking how the Rh3+ diffusion coefficient in the electrolyte shifts. Worth doing since a space station or Mars outpost life-support system will need the same catalysts, but this is a proof that the plating step survives microgravity, not a new catalyst.

original_title: Case Report: Delayed cutaneous toxicity following accidental extravasation of trastuzumab emtansine via peripheral venous access in a patient with HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer
title: When the cancer drug leaks out of the vein instead of into it
blurb: A case report of a HER2-positive breast cancer patient whose T-DM1 infusion extravasated and caused severe, delayed-onset skin injury, despite the label calling these reactions mild to moderate. One more case adding to a pile that suggests the label is underselling it.

original_title: Prediction of PD-L1 status and characterization of tumor subtype in NSCLC with static and abbreviated dynamic LAFOV [18F]FDG PET
title: Guessing PD-L1 status off a PET scan instead of a biopsy
blurb: In 51 treatment-naive NSCLC patients, a 20-minute dynamic FDG PET scan on a long axial field-of-view scanner told adenocarcinoma apart from squamous cell tumors and predicted PD-L1 status without cutting anyone open. Small cohort, but if it replicates that's a needle you don't need.
venue: European Journal of Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging

original_title: Radiosynoviorthesis in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis.
title: Radiosynoviorthesis for rheumatoid arthritis, revisited
blurb: A look at radiosynoviorthesis, injecting a radioisotope directly into an inflamed joint, as an RA treatment.
venue: Q J Nucl Med Mol Imaging

original_title: A multi-pathway kinetic framework to correct real-time-storage extrapolation biases in biopharmaceuticals
title: Patching the math behind drug shelf-life extrapolation
blurb: A multi-pathway kinetic framework meant to correct the bias that creeps in when real-time storage data gets extrapolated out to predict a biologic's actual shelf life. No numbers here to say whether it actually fixes the problem.

original_title: MS2-KNN: A Computational Framework Resolving Chimeric Small-Molecule MS/MS Spectra by Latent-Space Neighborhood Decomposition and Scaffold Confidence Scoring
title: Untangling MS/MS spectra when two molecules coelute into one scan
blurb: MS2-KNN embeds chimeric MS/MS spectra, the ones wrecked by precursor coisolation, into a shared latent space, pulls top-K candidates, prunes the unlikely ones by similarity, then scores what's left by scaffold confidence. The point is replacing single-precursor library search, which was never going to work once two compounds are stacked in the same isolation window.

original_title: An Intelligent Radio-Theranostic Dual-Lock Nanotransducer for Amplified Tumor-Targeted CR-PDT With Suppressed Normal-Tissue Toxicity.
title: A nanoparticle that won't fire until it's sure it's inside the tumor
blurb: A dual-lock radio-theranostic nanotransducer built to only trigger its CR-PDT effect once it's confirmed it's sitting in the tumor, which matters because amplifying the photodynamic effect usually means amplifying the damage to everything around it too.
